You are a developer community manager. You want to survey your community about their video preferences, analyze which programming topics get the most engagement on the Fireship channel, create an online survey form for the community, compile video statistics into a spreadsheet, and schedule a community call. The community manager at community@devclub.io has asked you to prepare this monthly engagement report.

Your workflow should proceed as follows.

First, search the video platform for Fireship videos. Across all programming topics on the channel (which span JavaScript, TypeScript, React, AI and machine learning, systems programming, DevOps and others), select the eight videos with the highest view counts. For each video, collect the video identifier, title, view count, like count, duration in seconds, and a primary topic tag derived from the video's content theme.

Second, create a spreadsheet file named Community_Report.xlsx. In the first sheet named Top_Videos, include the following columns in order: Rank, Video_ID, Title, Views, Likes, Duration_Sec, Topic_Tags. Populate this sheet with one row per video, ranked from highest to lowest by view count, with Rank starting at 1. Also compute the engagement rate for each video as likes divided by views multiplied by 100, and include this as an additional column named Engagement_Rate. In a second sheet named Engagement_Analysis, include the following columns: Topic, Avg_Engagement_Rate, Total_Views, Video_Count. Populate it with one row per distinct topic, aggregating the videos by their Topic_Tags. There should be at least 4 topic rows.

Third, create an online survey form titled "Fireship Community Preference Survey". Add the following questions to the form. The first question should ask "Which Fireship topic interests you most?" as a single-choice radio question with these options: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, AI and ML, Systems and Rust, DevOps and Cloud, Other. The second question should ask "How often do you watch Fireship?" as a radio question with options: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Rarely. The third question should ask "What format do you prefer?" as a radio question with options: Short under 5 minutes, Medium 5 to 15 minutes, Long over 15 minutes. The fourth question should ask "Your current role" as a radio question with options: Student, Junior Developer, Senior Developer, Engineering Manager, Other. The fifth question should ask "What topic should Fireship cover next?" as an open text question.

Fourth, check the shared calendar for any existing community events in April 2026. Then create a new calendar event titled "Community Standup" scheduled for April 1 2026 from 18:00 to 19:00 UTC.

Fifth, send an email to community@devclub.io. The subject should reference the monthly engagement report. The body should summarize the top video topics, mention the engagement rates found, provide the survey form identifier so members can access it, and note the community standup scheduled for April 1.

The configuration file in your workspace is named community_config.json and contains the target topics and report title. A report template named report_template.md explains the column formats, how engagement rate is calculated, and the ranking logic.

When all outputs are complete, claim the task as done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. This top-eight report, five-question form, one meeting, and one email are compact and share one small fact table.

Dynamically resolve and read `community_config.json` plus `report_template.md`; freeze the channel, ranking, taxonomy, engagement units, workbook headers, exact form wording/options/flags, email contract, and UTC standup. Run one complete read-only Fireship catalog session: obtain one channel list identifier, navigate only that identifier sequentially to exhaustion, fetch needed details, rank all observed videos by integer views with stable Video_ID tie-break, select exactly eight, assign one evidence-supported primary topic, and compute `likes/views*100` once. Freeze the top-eight and topic aggregates. Create `Community_Report.xlsx` once with exact `Top_Videos` and `Engagement_Analysis` headers, literal values, at least four supported topic rows, and consistent aggregates; read both sheets back.

Call `list_events` over April 1, 2026 with sufficient `maxResults` and `orderBy="startTime"`, filter exact `Community Standup` 18:00–19:00 UTC locally, create once only if absent with exact `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime`, retain its ID, and call `get_event`. Forms has no list/search: call `create_form` exactly once, never retry an ambiguous create, then append sequentially on the returned `formId` the four exact `add_multiple_choice_question` calls followed by the final exact `add_text_question`; never parallelize additions. Call `get_form` and verify title, five-question order/types/wording/options/flags. After workbook/form/event readback, check Sent mail and send one missing message to `community@devclub.io` with the exact subject, verified topics/rates, actual form ID, and UTC standup; read it back before `claim_done`.

You are planning a multi-step task for a developer community manager. Produce an ordered, detailed execution plan. Do NOT execute any mutations yourself — you are read-only. You may read files under the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-yt-fireship-gform-survey-excel-gcal/workspace (e.g. community_config.json, report_template.md) using mcp__local__ read tools, and you may inspect tool capabilities by listing what's available if needed.

TASK DESCRIPTION:
1. Search the video platform (YouTube MCP tools) for Fireship channel videos. Across all programming topics (JavaScript, TypeScript, React, AI/ML, systems programming, DevOps, etc.), select the EIGHT videos with the highest view counts. For each video collect: video identifier, title, view count, like count, duration in seconds, and a primary topic tag derived from the video's content theme. Note: the config file community_config.json contains target topics and the report title — use it.
2. Create spreadsheet Community_Report.xlsx in the workspace. Sheet 1 "Top_Videos": columns in order Rank, Video_ID, Title, Views, Likes, Duration_Sec, Topic_Tags, plus Engagement_Rate (likes/views*100). One row per video ranked highest-to-lowest by views, Rank starting at 1. Sheet 2 "Engagement_Analysis": columns Topic, Avg_Engagement_Rate, Total_Views, Video_Count — one row per distinct topic aggregated by Topic_Tags; must have at least 4 topic rows.
3. Create Google Form titled "Fireship Community Preference Survey" (via google_forms MCP tools) with these questions:
   Q1 radio "Which Fireship topic interests you most?" options: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, AI and ML, Systems and Rust, DevOps and Cloud, Other
   Q2 radio "How often do you watch Fireship?" options: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Rarely
   Q3 radio "What format do you prefer?" options: Short under 5 minutes, Medium 5 to 15 minutes, Long over 15 minutes
   Q4 radio "Your current role" options: Student, Junior Developer, Senior Developer, Engineering Manager, Other
   Q5 open text "What topic should Fireship cover next?"
4. Check the shared Google Calendar for existing community events in April 2026, then create a calendar event titled "Community Standup" on April 1 2026 18:00–19:00 UTC.
5. Send an email to community@devclub.io: subject references the monthly engagement report; body summarizes top video topics, mentions engagement rates found, provides the survey form identifier so members can access it, and notes the community standup on April 1.
6. Finally call mcp__local__claim_done.

YOUR DELIVERABLE: a step-by-step plan. For each step specify:
- Dispatch decision: self (main agent), explore, or coder.
- Whether the step is independent/parallelizable or must wait on a previous step's output.
- Key tool calls expected and any data-dependency notes (e.g. form ID needed for email body, video data needed for spreadsheet, etc.).
- Verification strategy for each artifact (e.g. re-read spreadsheet cells, list calendar events, get form details).

Also read community_config.json and report_template.md and incorporate their contents (target topics, report title, column formats, engagement rate formula, ranking logic) into the plan. Report what those files contain in your plan summary.
Plan the engagement report task

You are a read-only data collection agent. Your job: gather YouTube statistics for videos from the Fireship channel so the caller can pick the top 8 by view count.

CONTEXT:
- Fireship channel ID: UCsBjURrPoezykLs9EqgamOA
- Use only the mcp__youtube__ tools (channels_listVideos, channels_navigateList, videos_searchVideos, videos_getVideo, playlists_searchPlaylists, playlists_getPlaylistItems).
- Channel videos may span JavaScript, TypeScript, React, AI/ML, Rust/systems, DevOps/cloud, and other programming topics.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Enumerate the channel's videos. Try mcp__youtube__channels_listVideos with channelId "UCsBjURrPoezykLs9EqgamOA" and each sortOrder ("newest", "popular", "oldest"), maxResults 20, and navigate pages if pagination is supported (channels_navigateList with the returned listId). If the channel listing returns few/no videos, fall back to mcp__youtube__videos_searchVideos with queries like "Fireship", "Fireship JavaScript", "Fireship TypeScript", "Fireship React", "Fireship AI", "Fireship Rust", "Fireship DevOps", "Fireship Docker", "Fireship Python", "Fireship SQL", etc. Also try playlists_searchPlaylists("Fireship") then playlists_getPlaylistItems on promising playlists to discover more video IDs.
2. Build a candidate pool of Fireship video IDs (dedupe).
3. For as many candidates as feasible (aim for at least 20-40), fetch details with mcp__youtube__videos_getVideo(videoId, parts=["snippet","contentDetails","statistics"]). Record for each: video_id, title (from snippet.title), viewCount, likeCount, duration in SECONDS (contentDetails.duration may already be in seconds — if it looks like ISO 8601 like "PT12M34S", convert to seconds; if it is already a number of seconds, use it directly).

DELIVERABLE — return a structured report:
- A table of the TOP 20 videos by view count (descending), with columns: video_id | title | viewCount | likeCount | duration_sec.
- Also list the total number of unique candidate videos you evaluated and any videos whose stats could not be retrieved.
- If you could not reach 20 candidates, return everything you have, clearly stating the pool size.

Be precise with numbers — do not truncate or round view/like counts. Do not write any files; just report back.
Collect Fireship video stats
